claim: GlobalFoundries earns most of its revenue from finished wafers priced on a per-wafer basis for each customer design.
evidence: "The Company generates the majority of revenue from volume production and sales of finished semiconductor wafers, which are priced on a per-wafer basis for the applicable design." (Form 20-F FY2025, Summary of Material Accounting Policies, Revenue Recognition)

claim: Besides wafers, GlobalFoundries earns non-wafer revenue from NRE services, mask production, process qualification, post-fab bump/test/packaging services, and IP licences with royalties.
evidence: "We also generate non-wafer revenue from rendering non-recurring engineering (“NRE”) services, mask production, process qualification, post-fabrication services such as bump, test, and packaging, and revenue from intellectual property licenses and related royalties." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: GlobalFoundries recognises wafer revenue at a point in time, when wafers ship from its fab or are delivered to the customer, while NRE services are recognised over time on a cost-incurred basis.
evidence: "The performance obligations are satisfied at the point in which control of the wafers is transferred to the customer, which is determined to be at the point of wafer shipment from the Company’s facilities or delivery to the customer location." ... "NRE services are recognized over time as the Company performs the services based on a percentage of costs incurred over total expected costs." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: GlobalFoundries' master supply agreements can set volume-based pricing formulas, volume discounts and yield-adjustment calculations on top of purchase orders.
evidence: "The Company also enters into master supply agreements (“MSA”) with certain customers that may specify additional terms and conditions, such as pricing formulas based on volume, volume discounts, calculation of yield adjustments, indemnifications, transfer of title and risk of loss and payment terms." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: Some GlobalFoundries long-term supply agreements carry minimum volumes with a breakage fee if the customer does not meet the commitment; GF treats estimated breakage fees as variable consideration recognised with wafer revenue over the agreement term.
evidence: "For certain customers under long-term supply agreements (“LTAs”) with minimum volume requirements that are subject to a certain breakage fee if such commitment is not met" ... "The Company estimates for the breakage fee ... as variable consideration ... and accordingly, recognizes as revenue upon satisfaction of performance obligations for wafers over the expected term of the agreement." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: GlobalFoundries accrues volume rebates and yield adjustments, refundable to customers by credit note, as reductions of wafer revenue.
evidence: "The Company estimates the variable consideration related to volume rebates and yield adjustments for certain contracts that may be refundable to customers through the issuance of a credit note" (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: GlobalFoundries is typically paid 30-60 days after invoice, so it records no significant financing component on wafer sales.
evidence: "As a practical expedient, the Company does not adjust the amount of consideration for the effects of a significant financing component as payment is received shortly from the time the performance obligations are satisfied, which is typically between 30 and 60 days from the invoice date." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: GlobalFoundries recognises fixed-fee process-IP licence revenue at a point in time and related royalties when the licensee sells products using the technology.
evidence: "License revenue that is charged as a fixed fee is recognized at a point in time when the customer is provided with the right to use the license. Related royalty fees are recognized when the related sales of the product incorporating the licensed technology occur." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)

claim: TSMC recognises revenue when customers obtain control of goods, generally on delivery to the customer's specified location, net of estimated returns, rebates and allowances.
evidence: "The performance obligations are satisfied when customers obtain control of the promised goods, which is generally when the goods are delivered to the customers’ specified locations." "Revenue is reduced for estimated customer returns, rebates and other similar allowances." (Form 20-F FY2025, Summary of Material Accounting Policy Information, Revenue Recognition)

claim: TSMC's payment terms are in principle 30 days from invoice or 15 days after the end of the invoice month.
evidence: "In principle, payment term granted to customers is due 30 days from the invoice date or 15 days from the end of the month of when the invoice is issued." (Form 20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition)
